description_full: OUTFRONT Media Inc. is one of the largest and most trusted out-of-home media companies in the U.S., helping brands connect with audiences in the moments and environments that matter most. As OUTFRONT evolves, it's defining a new era of in-real-life marketing, turning public spaces into platforms for creativity, connection, and cultural relevance. With a nationwide footprint across billboards, digital displays, transit systems, and other out-of-home formats, OUTFRONT turns creative into powerful real-world experiences. Its in-house agency, OUTFRONT STUDIOS, and award-winning innovation team, XLabs, deliver standout storytelling, supported by advanced technology and data tools that can drive measurable impact. OUTFRONT Media Inc. was established in 2013 and was incorporated in Maryland.
ceo_bio: Mr. Nicolas  Brien | CEO & Director | Age 63 | Compensation: $1.7M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $925K ranks in the below the sector median among Real Estate peers. Each employee generates $110K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $15K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (3/10).
financial_summary: OUTFRONT Media Inc. is a mid-cap real estate business with a $5.9B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $219M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.09× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
